title: Cage: Hardware-Accelerated Safe WebAssembly
problem: WebAssembly applications written in unsafe languages lack memory safety guarantees despite WASM's sandboxing, and WASM's isolation mechanism incurs performance overhead.
motivation: Ubiquitous deployment of WASM across mobile, edge, and cloud domains necessitates stronger memory safety without sacrificing sandboxing performance.
method: Cage leverages Arm Memory Tagging Extension (MTE) to enforce spatial and temporal safety for heap and stack allocations, and uses Arm Pointer Authentication (PAC) to prevent pointer reuse across WASM instances. An LLVM-based compiler toolchain transforms unmodified WASM applications with function wrappers and metadata instrumentation.
key_novelty: First use of Arm MTE and PAC hardware features to provide memory safety and improve WASM sandboxing performance simultaneously.
contributions: Spatial and temporal memory safety for heap and stack allocations via MTE
Prevention of pointer reuse attacks via PAC
Minimal runtime (<5.8%) and memory (<3.7%) overheads on real hardware
baselines: Standard WASM runtime with default sandboxing
limitations: Evaluation limited to Arm-based systems with MTE/PAC support; generalization to other ISAs not discussed.
